Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to confirm a couple of items before we loop in legal:

1) On the private offer you shared, the list-price ladder shows a steep uplift at the 12-month commit. Can you provide a simple table that maps our commit buckets to effective unit prices (list price vs private offer)? We need to show this in our internal approval memo.

2) Our reseller (CoreHealth Distributors) wants written confirmation on the passback mechanics: how the reseller commission is computed and whether Redwood will honor a fixed reseller margin as part of the private offer.

If you can send the pricing table and a short note we can include with the PO, we’ll move Legal into a DocuSign review.

Cheers,
Sanjay

Hi Sanjay — thanks, and great question. See below and attached sheet. Short answers first:

• We’ll send a bucketized price table (attached) that shows list price, negotiated private-offer unit, and the blended effective rate by commit band.
• Redwood does not set reseller contract terms between HealthMetrics and CoreHealth; we can commit to the private-offer net price that you will pay (customer-facing price). If you need a written statement about the reseller commission calculation (passback % of list or a fixed $ per unit), our channel ops team can provide the standard passback template we use for marketplace private offers.

Action items I’m attaching: pricing csv (redwood-private-offer-pricing-sheet.csv) and a short passback-template draft. Ben — can you confirm the template language we send to distributors for passback guarantees? Irene — any constraints on us committing to a guaranteed reseller margin in writing here? Laura — I’ll need a one‑line on invoicing path (marketplace vs direct) for Sanjay’s PO memo.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-07-06T12:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer — requested anchor & channel math

Naomi / Irene —

Quick notes from channel ops: the passback-template reflects two common approaches we’ve seen: (A) % of list captured as a monthly rebate to distributor, or (B) fixed per-node uplift paid by Redwood as a cooperative marketing/passback credit. We usually default to option A for marketplace flows where listprice parity matters.

If HealthMetrics wants to lock in a guaranteed reseller margin to satisfy CoreHealth, we can offer a scoped guarantee for the term of the private offer but it requires:
- explicit reseller identity in the DocuSign exhibit (so we can enforce),
- a capped exposure (total passback not to exceed $X over 12 months), and
- signed acknowledgement from the reseller that they will not re-sell below the agreed net price.

Irene — any legal redlines on the wording? If not, we can produce a short Exhibit B showing the passback calculation and cap.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Channel Operations — Redwood Inference

(Attachment: passback-examples.xlsx)

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-07-07T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer — requested anchor & channel math

Thanks team —

Legally we should avoid promising the reseller a fixed margin payable by Redwood beyond a capped, demonstrable credit. Two suggested edits for the exhibit:
1) Define the passback as a customer-facing credit to HealthMetrics tied to verified invoice activity from CoreHealth; Redwood will calculate and remit the credit to HealthMetrics (or directly to CoreHealth via the approved channel routing).
2) Add a cap and recovery language — if HealthMetrics/Reseller requests retroactive proof beyond 90 days, we reserve the right to audit and adjust credits.

If HealthMetrics needs the margin guarantee solely for internal approval, we can provide a one‑page technical note describing how the calculation works and an illustrative scenario that shows the capped exposure. That usually satisfies procurement without us taking open-ended liability.

Laura — for invoicing path: if we route via AWS private-offer marketplace, invoices come through marketplace settlement (we provide listing evidence). If HealthMetrics prefers direct billing to Redwood (for faster reconciliation), the private offer can still be used as the pricing source but invoice will be direct — that has slightly different VAT/tax implications. Recommend we state both options and ask Sanjay which they prefer.

Irene Choi
Head of Legal — Redwood Inference
